- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates the continuation; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new trend; apply a 3–5% upward bias to early forecast points if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model tends to lag behind true price; add 1–3 days of lag correction by shifting forecast up 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-based adjustment.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; if sentiment turns negative after a spike, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
